title: Day 33 · Week 4, Day 5 — Protocol: the prenatal label, line by line — what has to be on it, what's usually missing, and the one ingredient that can hurt
summary: The first Protocol episode, promised on Day 29. Your baby is crossing from Carnegie stage 8 to 9 — 1.5 to 2.5 mm, the neural plate folding, the first one to three somite pairs, the cardiogenic region organising — and every one of those is a nutrient story. Six steps. What a supplement label is (the FDA does not approve or test supplements before sale; the USP Verified mark is the independent check). Folic acid: 400–800 µg, USPSTF grade A; 667 µg DFE is the same dose; the CDC's flat statement that MTHFR variants are not a reason to avoid folic acid. The two lines most often missing: iodine (76% of 188 prenatals, median 150 µg; 63% of US pregnant women below the sufficiency threshold) and choline (40% of products, median 25 mg against a 450 mg target; 7.7% of pregnant women meet it). The four lines with trials: iron (anaemia at term −70% in 43,274 women), vitamin D (600 IU; moderate-certainty hints on pre-eclampsia), calcium (food; supplements help low-intake populations), and DHA (early preterm birth 4.6% → 2.7% in 70 RCTs; nothing measurable for IQ). The red line: preformed vitamin A above 10,000 IU a day — prevalence ratio 4.8 for cranial neural crest defects in 22,748 women, before the seventh week, about 1 affected infant in 57. Prescription prenatals have fewer vitamins and minerals, not more. And the 2023 audit of 20,547 supplements that found exactly one product with all six key nutrients at target doses, not a prenatal, at about $200 a month and seven tablets a day. The nine-line check to run tonight.
action: Tonight, bottle in one hand and phone in the other, run the nine lines: USP seal; folic acid ≥400 µg (667 µg DFE) and <1,000 µg; iodine 150 µg as potassium iodide; choline (note it, expect little; plan eggs or ask about a separate supplement); iron ~27 mg, under 45, with vitamin C and apart from calcium; vitamin D ≥600 IU, under 4,000; calcium from food; DHA ≥200 mg or fish twice a week; vitamin A ≤770 µg RAE of retinol or mostly beta-carotene. Photograph the supplement-facts panel for the first visit. If iodine is missing, order 150 µg potassium iodide tonight and switch to iodised salt; if the vitamin A is retinol in the thousands of micrograms, replace the bottle tomorrow. Add eggs and a lower-mercury fish to this week's shopping.
